about: This three-panel version of Tuxedo Winnie the Pooh escalates refinement step by step. At the top, plain Pooh sits slumped in a blue armchair in his usual red shirt. In the middle he wears a tuxedo with a smug, half-lidded smile. At the bottom he adds a black bowler hat, a monocle and a curled mustache, looking absurdly aristocratic. Each panel pairs with a fancier way of saying the same thing, so the joke builds into a final, ridiculously pompous wording.
origin: The plain Pooh image comes from Disney's Winnie the Pooh animation of the 1970s, and the tuxedo edit spread as a "fellow man of culture" reaction image before taking off on Reddit around March 2019. The three-panel version adds a third, even posher tier.
usage:
Fill the three boxes to the right of Pooh from most basic to most extravagant. The top box gets the everyday word, the middle box a fancier synonym, the bottom box an over-the-top, pretentious or absurdly technical phrase. Example: "cat", "feline", "small tiger".

The third panel is the punchline, so make it the strangest and most elaborate. It works for jargon, brand names, job titles, food, and the wordy way people describe simple things to seem smart.
